factors.name: Size and branching volume
factors.summary: Very high loadings of Token split, Number of empty sequence flows, Control flow complexity, Size and Coefficient of network connectivity (0.90–0.97) show that larger nets in this dataset also have more splits, more parallel branching and more arcs per node. Maximum connector degree (0.76, with 0.39 on Factor 2) and Connector Mismatch (0.55, communality only 0.35) join more weakly. Density loads negatively (-0.46), which fits density shrinking as nets grow.

factors.name: Connector degree and density
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.89) and Density (0.84) load together, while Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.58). The factor describes nets whose connectors have many arcs relative to net size, with a more uniform mix of connector types. Density also has a secondary loading of -0.46 on Factor 1, and Connector Heterogeneity has a low communality (0.35).

factors.name: Sequential, separable structure
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.96) and Separability (0.69) define this factor, which captures how far a net consists of plain sequences and decomposes at articulation points. It rests on only two measures. Sequentiality shows a possible Heywood case (communality 1.017), so the factor is not well identified.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.83, so the 12 measures are suitable for factor analysis. Three varimax-rotated factors explain 82% of the variance, in line with three eigenvalues above 1 (6.81, 2.31, 1.20). A dominant size-and-branching factor (49%) is followed by a connector degree/density factor (17%) and a sequentiality/separability factor (16%). All measures are assigned and there are no flagged cross-loadings, but several measures have secondary loadings of 0.3–0.46 and the third factor is weak.
caveats: Sequentiality has a communality above 1 (possible Heywood case), so the third factor and its loadings should be read with caution.
Factor 3 rests on only two measures, and its eigenvalue (1.20) is only just above 1.
Connector Mismatch and Connector Heterogeneity have low communalities (about 0.35), so the factors represent them only partially.
Number of duplicate tasks was constant and removed, so the analysis says nothing about duplicate labels.

Several measures have secondary loadings, for example Density (-0.46 on Factor 1), Maximum connector degree (0.39 on Factor 2) and Coefficient of network connectivity (0.35 on Factor 3), so the factors are not cleanly separated.
The structure reflects shared variance in these 288 discovered nets under varimax rotation with three factors and may differ for other data or settings.
